prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. PRODUCTION REFERENCE SHEET, landscape, not a finished book page. Bold clean clear 2D children's cartoon throughout, crisp continuous dark outlines, flat clean colors, restrained smooth cel shading, no painted or grainy texture, no gouache, no embossed relief, no 3D. Original friendly readable illustration. Ordinary neutral settings; no flags, religious/political symbols or costumes. No logos, text, letters, numbers, pseudo-writing, captions, watermarks or page borders. Natural anatomy and coherent hand/prop contact. Essential content at least 8 percent inside every edge.
WD-KIT / Kit: six-year-old human boy, golden light-medium skin, short straight black side-parted hair, teal T-shirt, mustard shorts, navy sneakers. The ONLY named human protagonist is Kit. Zoe MUST NOT appear. Ignore every other child shown in reference sheets; unnamed adults may appear only when this scene explicitly requires them. Preserve exact reference identity and clothing.
Book: Ice in a Dish; World Discovery; nonfiction.
Setting: A warm indoor room in daylight. One shallow white dish with a teal rim stays on a flat pale table. No added water, hot plate or heat source; the room and table warm the ice.
Design locks for the book's recurring subjects/props (NOT a visibility list; never insert later objects/states prematurely): One clear cubical ice piece initially about three centimeters wide; One shallow round white dish with teal rim and room around the cube; Kit in locked clothes observes; both hands visible only when setting or tilting the dish; The amount of remaining ice decreases as its meltwater grows; no new ice appears
 Create a clean separated reference board on white: show the principal recurring props/animals in front, side and three-quarter views, their relative scale beside any named human cast, and a single simple location key showing the persistent setting and daylight/palette. The human character model sheet is a supporting identity reference, not content to copy wholesale. Show only the subjects this book requires. Use initial object states: One cube; dish initially dry; no poured water.. For orientation, the opening location/action is: Close three-quarter view of one intact clear cube in the dry center of the white dish. Kit’s two hands have just set the dish down and rest clear of the cube.. Do not show a completed craft or later scene merely because the finished object is listed in design locks. No future story events, no captions.
Production finish: every surface must be perfectly flat, clean digital cel color with smooth crisp outlines. ZERO paper grain, speckling, stipple, dither, paint, canvas fibers, mottling, scuffs or noisy gradients anywhere, including skin, rug, walls, table, floor and shadows. Prefer solid flat fills; any small shadow is one smooth flat shape. This is polished vector-like raster art, never a textured watercolor print.

visualReview.note: Inspected regenerated reference board: one small intact clear cube, shallow white dish with teal rim, Kit in locked clothes and warm room palette. Cube is suitably small relative to hand and dish; initial cube is dry, no melting sequence or extra water included. Continuous outlines and clean digital fills.
